components.text: Microsoft is still clearly positive, but 23% lower than a year ago. It expects positive free cash flow in fiscal 2027.

footnote: Source: Microsoft call, company releases (Jul 2026), Oracle filings (Jun, Sep 2026). Each firm's own definition
notes: Free cash flow here follows each company's own definition and the periods differ, so read the direction, not a ranking. Alphabet was minus $5.9bn in Q2 against plus $5.3bn a year earlier, and in the same quarter it announced an $84.75bn equity package. Amazon reports a trailing twelve-month figure, minus $7.6bn, which some outlets misread as a single quarter. Meta had $0.78bn left in Q2. Oracle's fiscal year ends in May: minus $23.7bn for fiscal 2026 and minus $5.4bn in the June to August quarter, and that quarter's operating cash included $11.4bn of customer prepayments. Microsoft made $19.6bn in calendar Q2, 23% less than the $25.6bn a year earlier, and says free cash flow stays positive in fiscal 2027.
